notes: Modified cash basis audit. Governmental: Statement of Revenues Received, Expenditures Paid and Changes in Fund Balances (pp4-5), Total Governmental Funds column. Fund balance roll-forward ties: 1,004,594 + 835,311 - 2,351,842 + 263,443 - 226,000 + 1,545,000 = 1,070,506. Cash and fund balance are separate measures: beginning/ending cash are the printed Cash and cash equivalents of the governmental funds statement (2022 comparative 801,509; 2023 1,016,048, p3), investments separately (248,366 / 110,282); the cash figures do not roll forward on receipts/disbursements alone because of interfund balances and investment changes. Proceeds of refunding bonds 1,545,000 (Street Fund) recorded as debt_proceeds; the Street budget schedule shows the 940,000 principal as 'Bond payments' under other financing, while the fund statement counts it in Debt service Principal (detail kept as printed). Sales and miscellaneous taxes = Sales taxes on the Statement of Activities (222,832, p2). Business-type: proprietary Statement of Revenues, Expenses and Changes in Net Position - Modified Cash Basis (p7), same basis and totals as the Statement of Activities (expenses 528,696, charges 474,953, interest 1,810, transfers (37,443), net position 2,436,714 -> 2,347,338); other operating revenues 1,319 counted in charges for services per the Statement of Activities. Proprietary cash flows from p8 Total column. Balance sheet: government-wide Statement of Net Position - Modified Cash Basis (p1), since it carries internal balances and business capital assets that the governmental funds statement does not (funds statement shows gross due from/to other funds). Detail: budgetary comparison schedules for every governmental and proprietary fund (pp9-19); zero-actual lines omitted; Park & Rec, Keno and Garbage print no revenue total line; Keno has no expenditures. Transfers: General out 226,000 = Police 42,000 + Fire 30,000 + Library 38,000 + Park & Rec 116,000; Sewer out 37,443 -> Debt Service; Garbage out 10,000 -> Sewer. Read pages 1-19 of 19
